clue.text: "White tie with hot pants" ad redesigned to cover backside

indicators.note: the letters of the ad are laid out afresh
the rearranged letters sit over and around the next piece

parts.note: HOT PANTS AD rearranged, ten letters

explanation.surface: A cheeky fashion advert has been redone so that its hot pants now cover the model's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: White tie is the most formal British dress code: a tailcoat with a white bow tie, traditionally worn with a top hat.
explanation.definitionFit: White tie is the dress code whose outfit is a top hat and tails.

clue.text: Beasts destroyed gorse

indicators.note: the word gorse is wrecked and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: Some animals have trampled and ruined a patch of gorse bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub common on British heaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are monstrous brutes, so beasts in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Harry takes winter vehicle, skipping Germany

parts.note: has = takes, as in 'has a biscuit'
SLED minus D, the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Prince Harry commandeers a sled for a winter trip but gives Germany a miss.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like the prince, but it is the verb: to harry is to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to hassle them with constant demands.

clue.text: Most eager characters taken in by artist Hirst, I estimate

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone guesses at which letters the artist Damien Hirst has absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Damien Hirst is the British artist of the pickled shark; his name conveniently supplies most of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty can mean eager, as in thirsty for knowledge, so thirstiest is most eager.

clue.text: What Islington postcode starts with zero?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: Islington, in north London, has the postcode N1, which written out is N plus the word for 1
second meaning: not any, nothing at all

explanation.walkthrough: London postcodes are a compass letter plus a number; Islington's is N1, and spelling the figure out gives the answer. 'Starts with' only joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: None means not any at all, which is a quantity of zero.

clue.text: However casually, hugging friend results in charge!

indicators.note: the casual word wraps its arms round the friend

parts.note: tho' is an informal spelling of though, meaning however

explanation.surface: A sentimental tale: an embrace between friends ends in a criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The charge is not a legal one: tally-ho is the huntsman's cry as the hounds are sent after a fox, used generally as a rallying shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the cry that sends riders charging after a sighted fox.

clue.text: Lead-free facilities prepared for bank on paper

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, put into a new form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lead-free means without its lead, its leading letter, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written: the word whose first letter goes

explanation.surface: Unleaded fuel stations have been readied, perhaps to lend money on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead-free' removes the F from facilities, and 'prepared' rearranges ACILITIES. To bank is to tilt, as a plane does, so slanted print is banked type.
explanation.definitionFit: To italicise is to set text in sloping type, so it makes letters lean, or bank, on the page.

clue.text: Go out more, avoiding unknown creep when talking tough stuff

parts.note: STAY IN LESS = go out more, minus Y, an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: to steal = to creep, as in steal into a room

explanation.surface: Advice to a shut-in: get out more and stop lurking about speaking tough.
explanation.walkthrough: STAY IN LESS is a roundabout way of saying go out more; dropping the Y takes it to the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stainless steel is a hard, durable metal alloy: tough stuff.

clue.text: Disorderly teen's breaking a raw academic member's connection

indicators.note: breaking means splitting apart, so the rearranged letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, an academic

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: anagram fodder, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An unruly teenager disrupting a cold, uncomfortable professor.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in teen's is ignored for the anagram. The surface's academic member sounds like a faculty member, but the member is a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon attaches the calf muscles to the heel bone, a connection in the leg, a limb or member.

clue.text: One believes appeal Sir Humphrey's opening looks retrograde in pen

indicators.note: the three pieces appear running backwards
the turned-round string goes inside the pen

parts.note: can = prison (pen); HRISTI goes between C and AN
it = sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A civil servant's charm fades as the TV mandarin Sir Humphrey writes in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Humphrey is the scheming civil servant of the British TV comedy Yes, Minister. Pen and can are both slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a follower of Christ is, above all, someone who holds a faith.

clue.text: Doe-eyed creature's all over relative

indicators.note: turned over, so written backwards

parts.note: taken as it stands, then flipped to LLA

explanation.surface: Someone with big soft eyes is fawned over by the whole family.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a contraction of is, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are famous for their large, long-lashed eyes.

clue.text: Piano's quality's occasionally lacking, causing aspersions

indicators.note: every other letter goes missing

explanation.surface: A concert review: the piano's tone kept faltering and drew harsh remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes are ignored; strike alternate letters from PIANOSQUALITYS starting with the P.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions is to throw insults at someone.

clue.text: Scarcity's hollowed out Iran — I must move from Middle East

indicators.note: the I shifts position within IRAN
only the shell of the word is kept

parts.note: IRAN with its I moved one place along

explanation.surface: A news line about shortages in a gutted Iran, whose people must flee the region.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in IRAN only hops one place, from first to second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is in the Middle East, so Syrian means from there.

clue.text: Planned to feature in Lancet: "Are bile ducts twisted?"

indicators.note: the answer appears inside the quoted words
the hidden letters run backwards

parts.note: lancET ARE BILE Ducts, read from right to left

explanation.surface: A headline from The Lancet medical journal asking whether bile ducts can get kinked.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lancet is a British medical journal, which makes the anatomy look like the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something planned was done on purpose, intentionally.

clue.text: Run out of cannabis with 90 per cent reduction initially

indicators.note: the first letter, a Roman numeral for 500, is cut by ninety per cent to the numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A dealer runs short of cannabis after his supply is slashed by ninety per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals D is 500 and L is 50, so 'with 90 per cent reduction initially' turns the D at the front of DOPE into L.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy, bounding strides.

clue.text: Possible way to get lolly stick more frozen?

explanation.surface: An ice-lolly riddle: what makes the stick even colder?
explanation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for money, not an ice lolly; NUMBER must be read as numb-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Keying in a PIN number at a cash machine is one way to withdraw money.

clue.text: Work regime that could mean four being cut

definitions.meaning: a drop of four, as when one number is lowered to a smaller one

explanation.surface: A job that could involve four staff being laid off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is arithmetic: nine down to five is a cut of four.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine-to-five describes the usual office working day.

clue.text: No safety net and no rubber ring?

definitions.meaning: the figurative reading: nothing to catch you if you fail
the literal reading: someone dropped in water with no float

explanation.surface: A swimmer, or a trapeze artist, facing the water with nothing to catch them.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, a non-swimmer without a rubber ring must sink or swim; figuratively, no safety net means succeeding or failing unaided.
explanation.definitionFit: Sink or swim describes a situation where you succeed or fail with no help.

clue.text: Old saint substantially funded this African native's fast

explanation.surface: A wealthy old saint bankrolled an African native's fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast looks like going without food, but it is speed: the ostrich is the fastest bird on land.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is native to Africa, and famously fast.

clue.text: Margaret briefly flipped about son's sparklers

indicators.note: turned round, so written backwards

parts.note: Meg is a short form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret briefly lost her temper over her son's fireworks.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparklers look like the hand-held fireworks, but here they are jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Gems sparkle, so sparklers is a playful word for jewels.

clue.text: Man with self at heart in place of religion

indicators.note: only the core of the word is taken

parts.note: the middle two letters of sELf

explanation.surface: A man with his inner self at peace in a house of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: With looks like a link but joins the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship.

clue.text: Back street with neat vents

indicators.note: everything after it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A back street lined with tidy air vents.
explanation.walkthrough: Vents is a verb here, as a volcano vents; neat is used as of a spirit, unmixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that vents erupts, releasing lava and gas.

clue.text: Good day to cut former part in show

indicators.note: the greeting slices into the other pieces

parts.note: a greeting, placed between EX and BIT

explanation.surface: An actor has a good day as a former role is trimmed from the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Good day is a greeting, like hi, not a verdict on the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to put paintings on public display in a gallery.

clue.text: Set about panhandler, half knocked down, not out

parts.note: in = not out, as a batter still in

explanation.surface: A beggar is beaten half senseless and left not quite out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A panhandler is a beggar.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: set about a task means make a start on it.

clue.text: Sting starts on Stewart Copeland, Andy mediates

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Sting and Stewart Copeland fall out and Andy Summers steps in to make peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting, Stewart Copeland and Andy Summers were the three members of The Police, but Sting here is a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a sting is an elaborate confidence trick or swindle.

clue.text: Where many Arabic speakers are audible, ignoring the French rambling

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters are rearranged
ignoring says the named letters are left out of the pool

explanation.surface: Arabic speakers can be heard everywhere, except for some French people talking at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring' takes LE (the French) out of AUDIBLE to leave AUDIB, which 'rambling' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is a city and emirate in the United Arab Emirates, where Arabic is the official language.

clue.text: Feigned tenderness in speech toasted with this?

indicators.note: the words are to be heard, not read

explanation.surface: A wedding speech full of false affection, followed by the toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenderness is soreness here, not affection: pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the usual drink for a toast.

clue.text: No right digit found by emergency room — left also seeking location

explanation.surface: A patient missing a finger heads for the ER, but gets lost on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is England's northernmost county, on the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Northumberland is a place, a county of north-east England.
